patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] btrfs: fix double release of data space on failed direct IO COW write

version_history.subject: [PATCH] btrfs: fix double release of data space on failed direct IO COW write

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the Btrfs file system where data space is released twice when a direct IO COW write fails, leading to an underflow of bytes_may_use and potential warnings or clamping to zero. The fix involves recording the extent consumed by btrfs_reserve_extent() in dio_data and releasing only the remaining reserved data space from bytes_may_use on error paths. This patch can be applied to stable kernels later than v5.19, which rewrote the affected error path.

review_comments.summary: reviewer noted that on x86, shadow-stack PTEs have their ordinary write bit clear but pte_write() reports them writable due to shadow-stack instructions; this allows HMM to grant devices write access to the process's shadow stack, potentially corrupting return addresses or bypassing protection

Thanks.  This?

On x86, a shadow-stack PTE has its ordinary write bit clear.  The CPU
rejects ordinary stores, but pte_write() reports it writable because
shadow-stack instructions can write it.  HMM consequently sets
HMM_PFN_WRITE.  Nouveau uses that flag for GPU write permission, and
RDMA on-demand paging can use it to grant device write permission to a

potentially corrupting return addresses or bypassing that protection.

patches_reviewed.subject: Re: [PATCH] mm/hmm: skip NUMA balancing on protnone faults
patches_reviewed.patch_summary: Patch proposes to skip NUMA balancing on PROT_NONE faults, aiming to reduce GPU performance impact.

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (Meta)
review_comments.summary: Raised questions about the performance implications of mmu_notifiers in the presence of PROT_NONE faults, specifically whether the driver needs a global view of memory or just a subset.

review_comments.author: Alistair Popple
review_comments.summary: Clarified the process of GPU page table setup and mmu_notifier synchronization, explaining that the driver doesn't need a global view of memory but rather just a view of the memory it needs to access.
review_comments.raw_body:
On 2026-11-17 at 10:57 +1100, "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net> wrote...
> On 2026-11-17 10:24 +1100, Alistair Popple wrote:
> > On 2026-11-14 at 07:53 +1100, "Gregory Price (Meta)" <gourry@gourry.net> wrote...
> > > On 2026-11-13 21:43 +0100, David Hildenbrand (Arm) wrote:
> > > > On 11/13/26 21:34, Thomas Hellstrm wrote:
> > > 
> > > > I recall that John (cc) kept saying "GPUs and NUMA balancing is inherently
> > > > incompatible, you have to disable NUMA balancing".
> > > > 
> > > 
> > > If this is a NUMA-hotplugged GPU, then this is resolved by a private
> > > node, because this:
> > > 
> > > @@ -6404,6 +6404,9 @@ static vm_fault_t do_numa_page(struct vm_fault *vmf)
> > >         if (!folio || folio_is_zone_device(folio))
> > > 
> > > 
> > > changes to
> > > 
> > >         if (!folio || folio_is_common_memory(folio))
> > > 
> > > And all folios on the GPU node are never subject to NUMA Balancing
> > > 
> > > so balancing can stay enabled while the GPU memory is not subject to
> > > PROT_NONE spew.
> > 
> > Hi Gregory, just to hopefully help clarify understanding a bit here this isn't
> > related to folio location and therefore private node won't help much.
> > 
> > This about a driver getting a snapshot of current PTE state to program a
> > secondary MMU (in this case on a GPU, but can equally be a NIC or other device).
> > 
> > Even CPU memory being subject to NUMA balancing can have quite an adverse impact
> > on GPU performance due to increased incidence of GPU faults, hence why John says
> > GPUs (using SVM) are inherently incompatible with NUMA balancing.
> > 
> 
> Ah, I follow.  I'm still working through the performance implications of
> mmu_notifiers in the presence of PROT_NONE faults, but if i'm
> understanding correctly it tracks that you'd say it's incompatible.

Incompatible is probably not the correct term as it still works. It's just that
GPU faults are really expensive, and to be avoided at all costs. So having NUMA
balancing running around randomly unmapping pages the GPU is using (regardless
of whether or not they are on the device) results in more GPU faults and
therefore a huge perf impact for basically no (or in fact sometimes negative)
gain.

> I presume here the driver needs a global view of memory (or at least all
> memory it can potentially DMA), rather than simply just a subset
> (some set of VMAs)?

The basic process is this:

* GPU needs to access some user space virtual address (eg. allocated with mmap/malloc)
* Therefore GPU driver needs to setup GPU page tables to point to the physical
  memory[1] backing the user space virtual address
* To find the physical address the GPU driver uses hmm_range_fault() on the
  range, possibly faulting pages in if required (ie. if CPU PTE permissions
  don't match what's required).
* hmm_range_fault() relies on mmu_notifiers for synchronisation with CPU PTE state.
* An mmu_notifier firing causes a driver to do two things:
  a) Must invalidate any GPU page tables / TLBs mapping the notified virtual address.
  b) Increments a sequence number for any concurrent hmm_range_faults(), which must
     retry as their view of CPU PTEs is now out-dated. This is the problem
     this patch series hits - the migration on fault causes an mmu_notifier to fire
     resulting in a hmm_range_fault() retry and associated overhead.

So the driver doesn't need a global view of memory, just a view of the memory
the GPU needs, or likely needs, to access. Determining that depends on the
driver - some might require pre-registration of the ranges (eg. via an ioctl)
prior to launching work whilst others might wait until the GPU work faults on an
address not in the GPU page tables. Or some combination thereof.

 - Alistair

[1] - Well technically the IOVA / DMA address mapping physical system memory
but that's not relevant for this discussion. We can assume there are no IOMMUs
present.

> ~Gregory
> 
> -- 
> ~Gregory
> 
>

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH RFC] NFS: don't wait for writeback on close() with a write delegation

version_history.subject: [PATCH RFC] NFS: don't wait for writeback on close() with a write delegation

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFS client to no longer wait for writeback on close() when a write delegation is held, reverting behavior introduced by commit 5445b1fbd123. The change was made because waiting for writeback on close() provided no benefits and could lead to issues such as delayed error reporting and unnecessary flushing of data. Instead, the patch returns to the previous behavior where writeback is started on close() only when a write delegation is held. This change improves performance in certain scenarios, specifically single-threaded create/write/close operations against an NFS server with a nonzero space limit.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 1/4] mm: zswap: fix shrinker count for the root memcg
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the zswap shrinker, which incorrectly scales the number of freeable entries on the root memcg's zswap LRU by its compression ratio. The issue arises because the root memcg's stats do not account for its own zswap entries, leading to incorrect scaling and potential data loss. The patch uses the zswap pool-wide counters instead, ensuring that all zswap entries are accounted for.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 2/4] mm: memcg: read root lruvec stats from the node counters
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series modifies the way root memcg's lruvec stats are read, allowing for more accurate and up-to-date statistics by reading from node counters instead of rstat values in certain cases.

review_comments.author: Chris Down
review_comments.summary: Identified potential issues with the allowlist approach, suggesting that the changelog should specify which stats are on the list. Also pointed out a specific stat (NR_VMSCAN_WRITE) that may need to be added to the list.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

Joanne Koong writes:
>The exceptions are the kernel memory stats (slab, kernel stack, page
>tables, secondary page tables and vmalloc), hugetlb, and
>WORKINGSET_NODERECLAIM, which counts reclaimed xarray nodes (slab
>objects). Their node counters also count memory that isn't charged to a
>memcg, which falls into two categories:

This still describes the v2 denylist. With the allowlist, the root memcg
also keeps reading rstat for NR_ANON_MAPPED, NR_FILE_MAPPED, NR_SHMEM et
al, and some of those differ for reasons outside the two categories here,
like swapcache being counted differently in the node counter, for
example. Could the changelog say what is on the list instead? So that
would be the stats that only change through mod_lruvec_state(), with
everything else still reading rstat.

>+	case PGROTATE_ANON:
>+	case PGROTATE_FILE:
>+	case PGREFILL:
>+		return true;

NR_VMSCAN_WRITE isn't on the list, but prepare_scan_control() adds it to
WORKINGSET_RESTORE_ANON, so once the root flush in reclaim goes away,
root reclaim would mix a live node counter with a stale rstat value.
Unless I'm mistaken it should go here as well.

Once those are fixed, please feel free to add:

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

series_items.subject: [PATCH v3 3/4] mm: workingset: skip the root memcg flush in workingset_test_recent()
series_items.patch_summary: The patch modifies the workingset_test_recent() function to skip flushing the root memcg's statistics when the eviction memcg is also the root memcg. This optimization avoids an expensive flush operation on the refault path, which can take up to 0.9ms in systems with high cgroup activity.

review_comments.summary: Recommended using a mem_cgroup_flush_lru_stats_ratelimited() helper to simplify the code and make it easier to understand. Acknowledged that skipping the root flush is acceptable, but suggested keeping the original patch's logic in mind for future changes.

Hi Joanne,

Joanne Koong writes:
>-	if (flush)
>+	if (flush && !mem_cgroup_is_root(eviction_memcg))

Not a big deal, but in the v2 thread you mentioned you would try a

and at least speaking for myself, keeping the root check close to the list

to hold this patch up though, and I've tested that refaults in the root

Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] mm/page_alloc: drop unused gfp_mask from zone_watermark_fast()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch removes an unused argument from the zone_watermark_fast() function in the Linux kernel's page allocation module. The gfp_mask argument, which was introduced to check for atomic allocations, is no longer used since a previous commit switched the watermark boost check from __GFP_ATOMIC to ALLOC_MIN_RESERVE. The patch makes no functional changes and simply removes the unused argument.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] mm/page_alloc: move the kswapd node skip check into a helper
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the kswapd node skip check in the Linux kernel's page allocation code into a separate helper function called should_skip_kswapd_zone(). This makes the zone iteration cleaner and easier to read, while also resolving a checkpatch warning. The new function checks if kswapd is active on a node and if the zone is below its watermark for this request, and returns true if it should skip the zone. No functional changes are intended by this patch.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] mm/vmscan: consolidate promo vs. high watermark checks
series_items.patch_summary: This patch consolidates the pattern of checking the watermark that kswapd reclaims zones up to into a single helper function, reducing code duplication in three different sites. The function, `kswapd_wmark_pages`, takes into account whether NUMA balancing memory tiering is enabled and returns either the promo or high watermark accordingly. This change does not introduce any functional changes but simplifies the code by removing unnecessary includes and consolidating logic.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch set consists of three cleanups for the vmscan and page_alloc code, primarily aimed at making get_page_from_freelist easier to read. The changes include dropping an unused gfp_mask from zone_watermark_fast(), moving a kswapd node skip check into a helper function, and consolidating checks for promotion versus high watermark in vmscan. These cleanups are based on the latest page_alloc/for-next branch as of November 13, 2026, and do not introduce any functional changes.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/3] mm/page_alloc: move the kswapd node skip check into a helper
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the kswapd node skip check in the Linux kernel's page allocation code into a separate helper function called should_skip_kswapd_zone(). This makes the zone iteration cleaner to read and resolves a checkpatch warning. The function checks if kswapd is active on a node and if the zone is below its watermark for the current request, and returns false if so. This prevents accidental 'node_reclaim_mode'-like behavior when another process has NUMA bindings causing kswapd wakeups on only some nodes. No functional change is intended by this patch.

review_comments.author: Chris Down
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Chris Down noted that the should_skip_kswapd_zone() helper function does not handle the case where sysctl_numa_balancing_mode is set to NUMA_BALANCING_MEMORY_TIERING, and suggested adding a check for this condition.

Reviewer noted that the comment above the should_skip_kswapd_zone() function is misleading because it says kswapd is active when in fact waitqueue_active() being true means kswapd is asleep, and suggested rephrasing to reflect this.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Joshua,

Joshua Hahn writes:

---

Not a big deal, but now that the test is the other way round, this reads
backwards against "If kswapd is already active on a node" in the comment
above the function, because waitqueue_active() being true here means
kswapd is asleep on kswapd_wait. Maybe say something like that
kswapd is asleep, so nothing is reclaiming this? It needn't hold the patch
up though.

I've tested that this works well, so either way please feel free to add:

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>
Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Thanks!

Chris

series_items.subject: [PATCH 3/3] mm/vmscan: consolidate promo vs. high watermark checks
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series consolidates the logic for determining the watermark that kswapd reclaims zones up to, simplifying the code and removing unnecessary includes. The consolidation is done by introducing a new helper function `kswapd_wmark_pages` which returns either the promo or high watermark depending on whether NUMA balancing memory tiering is enabled.
